- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75), model often overshoots in subsequent days; apply downward correction of 2–5% for 2–3 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates; increase forecast by 1–4% to counteract mean reversion bias.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture mean reversion in 10–15 day horizons; apply a 1–3% downward adjustment if recent 7-day average is above 30-day average.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values before final output.
